body:
RESOLVED, using the script's own instrumentation rather than my reconstruction. I ran 05 as written, unmodified, UNCERTAINTY_NODES=25. Its own per-node timer:

  sampling covariance: 16.2 s total, 0.65 s/node mean
    first 10 nodes: 0.64 s/node, RSS 782 MB
    last 10 nodes : 0.57 s/node, RSS 557 MB

0.65 s/node, not ~9. All three claims in bd-01KZYYQCR3D7NDZQN5DN53AHRC's title checked against that output:

  ~7 s/node                  NOT REPRODUCED - 0.65 s/node by the script's clock, 0.455 s/node
                             by my independent reconstruction. Two methods, same order.
  appears to leak            REFUTED by the script's own RSS instrumentation. Per-node time
                             FALLS 0.64 -> 0.57 s, RSS FALLS 782 -> 557 MB. Both move the
                             wrong way for a leak.
  >1 h for 577 nodes         NOT REPRODUCED - 577 x 0.65 s is about 6.3 minutes.

single-node-only still holds, but that is a design property and at 0.65 s/node it is not the problem the bead describes.

AND A WARNING ABOUT MY OWN FIRST ATTEMPT, because it is in the log above and reads as confirmation. I ran the whole script under a 600 s limit, it exceeded it, and for a moment that looked like proof. It was not: the script's breakdown shows the covariance loop was 16.2 s of that total. The rest is data loading, the 577-centre frame build, the consistency RDM over all centres, and arms C and D. Timing a whole script and attributing the total to one function inside it is exactly the mistake I made twice earlier today, and I nearly made it a third time in the same thread.

FILED bd-01KZZSREBD26E7QGPMZF6K9CTS. The exemplar README Cost section says the arm costs ~9 s/node, 22 minutes for 120 nodes and 90 minutes for all 577. Measured: about 80 seconds and about 6.3 minutes. That section is the only place a user learns what a calibrated error bar costs, and the README already steers them away with 'Only 02-04 should be treated as the commit gate'. Pricing the capability at ten times its real cost will stop people using the thing an entire epic was built to provide.

ONE VERIFIED-GOOD FROM THE SAME RUN: 'refit RDM vs 02's precomputed-mean RDM: max abs difference = 4.44e-16'. The error-channel refit reproduces the point-estimate arm to machine epsilon - the guard the script says it needs, holding exactly.

I cannot establish WHEN this changed. The bead was filed at 01:38 and the tree has moved. The figure may have been right when written. I am reporting the current measured state, not adjudicating the original.
